lessons.text: Day 1: 9z beat Aurora 2-0, and Polymarket's own resolution record for cs2-9z-aur1-2026-10-14 (read into this project's capture at 23:50:48Z, resolution source hltv.org) records 9z as the winner. An upset is evidence of possibility; it is not proof that the pre-match price was wrong or that Aurora's July rebuild was unpriced in October.

Day 2: four BO3s - Aurora 2-0 NIP, Falcons 2-1 9z, BETBOOM 2-1 PARIVISION, FURIA 2-1 Legacy. Three of the four winners were the market side; the frozen pre-lock picks went 2/3 on the three archived matches, which is far too small a sample to claim an edge.

Day 3: both deciders were decided in two maps by the favourite (Aurora, priced about 1.40 by the relayed bc.game line recorded in hotspawn/research/day3_twc2026.json at 04:35Z) and in three maps by the underdog (BETBOOM, priced about 2.50 against Legacy 1.48). One day produced one favourite and one underdog, which is exactly what those prices imply; it is not a signal to fade or to chase favourites.

Aurora's kyxsan, Jimpphat and ash rebuild was reported on 8 July. It is about three months old, not last-minute onboarding, and no new injury, stand-in, travel or sleep claim is independently established.

Listing lesson for this project: as of 2026-10-16T23:52Z the main event has no pick'em surface on Hotspawn, so the semifinals stay research-only. The board never turns an unlisted fixture into a graded pick, and the four-hourly refresh will pick it up automatically if Hotspawn lists one.
Day 1: 9z beat Aurora 2-0 (Inferno + Nuke). The upset was real but context-specific: Aurora's veto was different and the July rebuild was just 3 months old.
Day 2: Aurora beat NIP 2-0; Falcons beat 9z 2-1; BETBOOM beat PARIVISION 2-1; FURIA beat Legacy 2-1. Both favourites who advanced had a scare (FURIA lost map 1, Falcons lost a map to 9z).

Day 3: Aurora swept 9z 2-0 (reversed Day 1 completely with a different veto). BETBOOM beat Legacy 2-1 in a tight three-map battle (Nuke OT, lost Dust2, won Mirage decider). Both day-3 winners advance to face rested opponents.

Aurora's kyxsan, Jimpphat and ash rebuild (July 8) is about 3 months old. The team has won 3 of last 5 series (including Spirit 2-0 and 1win 2-0) and showed strong LAN adaptation. The Day 1 upset was not a permanent weakness.

practical_rule: On a pickable fixture take the side with the larger source-backed probability and let the ownership differentiation decide only between close calls. On these two semifinals there is nothing to pick: the market is near-even in the first semi-final (so Aurora at 47% is not a fade) and unanimous in the second (Falcons 76-80%), where our own valve-points line is the outlier at 65.8% for Falcons.
limitations: Every price here is a dated capture from 2026-10-16T23:50:42Z-23:50:48Z; lines move and are re-read by the normal refresh, not by this file.
The semifinals are not Hotspawn fixtures in this capture, so no ownership sample exists and no leaderboard fade is defined for them.

Our own line is a two-parameter logistic on Valve's published points; it has no map-veto, LAN, preparation or fatigue calibration and is presented as an independent estimate, never as a bookmaker price.
Hotspawn's crowd ownership is stored and shown for pickable matches only as ownership, never as a probability.
Our own line is a match-level rating estimate from Valve's points: it has no map-veto, preparation, travel or fatigue term, and it is not a bookmaker quote.
HLTV's 'VRS' label on a match page can be newer than Valve's published file; the numbers used here are the 2026-10-05 published file, and any rank label copied from HLTV is quoted as HLTV shows it.

own_line_method.formula: P(A beats B) = 1 / (1 + 10 ** (-k * (points_a - points_b) / 400)) - this project's own line, never a bookmaker quote
own_line_method.k_source: calibrated on Valve's published results (hotspawn/data/calibration.json, generator hotspawn/calibrate.py)
own_line_method.applicability: The board applies this line only when the series format, both rosters and a fresh Valve snapshot pass the eligibility gates. These two semifinals have no Hotspawn row, so the same gates were re-checked by hand (see own_line_eligibility on each match) and the numbers are published as an estimate, with the outside market shown next to them.

contrarian_option_1.rationale: The captured books price Aurora at 47.0% (Pinnacle, margin removed), 50.0% (Thunderpick via bo3.gg) and 47.5% (Polymarket), and Aurora beat FURIA 2-1 at ESL Pro League Season 24 within the past 30 days (HLTV head-to-head panel). contrarian_option_1.ev_cost: Not computable: the fixture is not listed on Hotspawn, so no points are on offer.

contrarian_option_2.rationale: The books are unanimous that Falcons are a strong favourite (76.0% Pinnacle de-vigged, 76.9% relay, 79.5% Polymarket) and HLTV's crowd vote agrees (79.3%). Our own line disagrees by more than ten points - BETBOOM 34.2% - and BETBOOM are the only remaining team who played on 16 October, arriving from a three-map series. The raw 4.00 decimal relay price implies 25%, but the margin-removed two-way figure is 23.1%, so '25% versus a 13-17% market' from the merged draft was wrong.
contrarian_option_2.risk: High - short turnaround after a three-map decider, and only the model (not the books) rates BETBOOM above 24%.
contrarian_option_2.ev_cost: Not computable: the fixture is not listed on Hotspawn, so no points are on offer.

day4_contrarian_picks.recommended: With no Hotspawn listing for either semifinal, no expected-points decision exists and nothing here is a graded pick. If the fixture were listed, the supported side is the favourite in both games; Aurora is the more defensible contrarian (the books price the series near even) and BETBOOM only an occasional punt.
